_about: Roadmap progress. Each phase is a weighted list of items; weight is the item's share of that phase's effort, done its completion from 0 to 1. kind 'measured' means tools/progress.py computes done from the repository (or a census figure it records here); 'estimate' means a judgement, with its evidence. See docs/progress.md.

P1.item: Translation, lockstep, routes and the emulated PC (roadmap Phase 1 'Done')
P1.evidence: Batch ax (23 Oct 2026): all 17 game code files and the floating decompressor translated (89,433 instruction starts); instruction lockstep 0 mismatches over 5,723,136 compared states under each timing profile; 63 routes (62 fresh interpreter sessions) identical; 528 CTests pass. Earlier fidelity.py evidence: 1,210/1,210.

Settled by scope 8 Oct 2026 (roadmap 'Settled'): the weight is cut to the work done, dropping what was left. What was left (the test pilot's 7 of 9 over a +-15% stick-scale range on 86Box) measures the pilot, not the machines. Before: Done: tools/pc_parity.py checks pictures, music and the saved roster on both against measured limits, fidelity_all.py holds the machine probe, 86Box runs are deterministic (8 Oct 2026: the harness hook in the emulation thread; repeat runs byte-identical), the closed-loop supply drop delivers on both, a closed-loop career sortie saves its roster on both (DOSBox-X's and 86Box's byte-identical, ours differing only in the mission score, which END scores the same from either machine's handover), the 86Box intro drift and pitch-bend writes are explained, and the decision to use them as the routine references is made. The 86Box adaptor sends the stick as whole game frames (the game runs at about half the frame rate there), and the supply drop, the strike-training hit and the career landing then pass on 86Box too. Open: those flights pass 7 of 9 over a +-15% range of the one estimated stick scale, so a mission with a narrow window can still miss on 86Box.

P1.item: Rendered sound: speech and the PC speaker
P1.evidence: Scope 8 Oct 2026: matching DOSBox's OPL mixer sample for sample is dropped (the synthesis is the emulator's, the register stream the game's, and that is exact): every AdLib write of the intro matches GOG's capture in order and value (7 Oct). Speaker, shown 8 Oct 2026: the host runs PIT counter 2 clock by clock to the 8254 data sheet (src/host/speaker.c); the speaker driver's music, whose count rewrites the old renderer took at once (restarting the wave), now matches DOSBox-X's capture (tools/speaker_parity.py, intro 138 s: envelope 0.87, spectral 0.92-0.93, level 0.95; before 0.69, 0.54, 0.47), with its 736 gate changes and 440 control words identical; the radio call (counter 2 mode 0 PWM, 79-clock carrier) has its 12,924 counts identical to DOSBox-X's and renders carrier-free (realsound, default) or as the pulse train (pwm); in band it equals GOG DOSBox's count-as-level model (|r| 0.97, equal energy). Shown 9 Oct 2026 on 86Box's MS-DOS 5.00 VMs (b86_cargo_pilot.py --profile, B86_OPL / B86_SPKLOG): the takeoff call's 6,464 AdLib register-43h writes and the speaker driver's 13,046 counts are identical in order and value to this machine's, at the same rate (7,938 vs 7,936 writes a second; 15.1 counts a millisecond). Open (weight 0.23 of 5.6): an audio reference for the speech (DOSBox-X plays none of it); listening is Phase 4. Closed 9 Oct 2026: independent silent 86Box mixer capture (86box-audio.patch, speech_audio.py), MS-DOS 5.00/MOUSE.COM 6.26, speaker driver. Identical 12,924 non-silence takeoff-call counts, 855.6255 ms. In 300-3400 Hz, waveform correlation -0.991565, envelope 0.999516, zero lag and ours/reference RMS 3.16856; polarity and gain follow PIT duty (10000/79 per count) versus 86Box count-as-level (10240/256). In 100-8000 Hz correlation -0.988890, envelope 0.999437. Capture off/on has byte-identical 4,500 frame records, 1,621 AdLib writes and speaker port log. Reports repeat identically; altered count stream is rejected. This supplies the missing waveform reference; listening remains Phase 4. See tools/ref86box/build_86box.md. No runtime/default changes.

Completed 10 Oct 2026. Both engines charge the same 386DX/33 profile; all 93 probe blocks match the saved MS-DOS 5.00/MOUSE.COM 6.26 reference (AH=2Ch varies by four cycles); 5.7M instruction comparisons, repeated with code in VRAM, have zero differences including prefetch and held REP state. Paired flights have 574 identical checkpoints and stick responses. STI/SS-load shadows include zero-cycle instructions; four regressions pass. Matched entries run translated bodies under this profile. File services, EXEC and overlays are charged at the reference period disk's measured costs. The last alleged hold failure compared a default 9 MIPS capture against 86Box. Retained profile/content-aware checks and fresh full references now pass: all 21 local held pictures match, max duration difference 0.214 s (limit 0.35), drift 1.113 s (limit 2.2), final hangar 19 ms apart. Pictures, music and both roster saves pass too. Eight regression tests protect profile identity, matching and timing verdicts. Direct cycle charges in handwritten routines remain an optional performance improvement.

P3.item: Stage 4: live feed, pacing, threading and 4K throughput
P3.evidence: Live draw feed (drawfeed.c), host pacing at vsync on the machine clock, picture-age setting, original-picture switch, threaded presentation (records replayed as they arrive, in-between work one frame ahead on a worker, palette on helper threads). Isolated fullscreen D3D11 3840x2160/59.99 Hz/N=9 runs passed tools/presentation_timing.py on strike, air-to-air and landing (13 Oct; p99 16.71 ms) with every logic frame exact; hidden 4K throughput 119-150 fps (15 Oct). Fullscreen 4K/59.99 Hz timing of the latest build (rerun, 17 Oct 2026, owner screen): strike and landing pass (p99 16.95 and 17.38 ms); air-to-air fails the p99 limit on a short sample (22.15 ms, 0.42% over 25 ms), so no credit yet. The authorized longer air-to-air check (17 Oct) also fails: 17,241 pictures, p99 28.6976 ms, 3.7022% over 25 ms; all 3,679 logic frames exact and guest drift 0.005819 s. No score increase. Open: diagnose pacing, slower CPUs/weaker GPUs, cargo/career flights. Evidence: D:/f117-gate/present-v2/stage4-airair-long-20261017. Reused by the new 60+ fps method. Capacity on long flights and fewer cores (19 Oct 2026, hidden, this machine): four whole flights (cargo_return and career_promotion legacy; landing and strike at 15 Hz / 60 MIPS, 17.9-30 min) keep per-minute median main work 5.2-10.2 ms with worst one-minute p99 18.4 ms and nothing over 25 ms in the heaviest combat minute; pinned to 4/2 CPUs p99 15.6/16.0 ms, to 1 CPU 20.87 ms (a proxy for a slower machine); a software renderer fails (p99 43 ms; a proxy for no GPU acceleration). Raised from 0.90 to 0.97 on 19 Oct, then to 1.0 after the announced fullscreen long-flight run (19 Oct, owner's 4K screen, 15 Hz / 60 MIPS landing pilot recording, 24 minutes: 64,338 flight pictures, interval median 16.6676 ms, p99 16.9513 ms, maximum 21.4635 ms, zero missed, drift 10 ms, 16,088 logic frames and the final hash exact). The owner's visual judgement of the motion is not claimed and stays with him. Other physical machines, other refresh rates and the owner's visual judgement moved to Phase 4 as a maybe (owner, 18 Oct). See presentation.md.

Lowered 15 Oct 2026 from 0.85 (as one item with Stage 4): the owner judges the interpolated motion not acceptable (roads jitter, objects jump). What exists: primitive-pairing interpolation, exact at both ends of every step on all 45 routes; tools/motion_check.py measures pairing, deformation and step-timing irregularity; the step-clock cause found and a smoothed playback clock simulated (freezes/skips 35 -> 2). Identity pairing was tried and turned off (it deformed objects). The replacement is integrated as --present rerun, with the full gate and all 45 rerun N=1 routes exact; 1,638,579 copy-isolation checks keep real memory/machine/fix state unchanged: the original's unmodified draw on a throwaway machine copy with nudged camera/object inputs, refined at any scale, plus the smoothed clock. Hidden owner-flight runs reduce freezes and speed changes; skips, parallel copies for high refresh rates and the owner's physical-display motion verdict remain open. Owner verdict 15 Oct 2026 (22:32), after playing 4k-rerun.bat fullscreen at 4K twice: "seems great" apart from the original's own jitter, "looks good" after the threaded-palette fix, "good at least for now": raised to 0.9. Remaining (17 Oct 2026): clock skips against picture age and slower machines. Refresh rates above 60 Hz (per-machine state for parallel copies) moved to Phase 4 on 17 Oct 2026 and are not scored: the owner has no convenient high-refresh display to test on. Done was raised from 0.9 to 0.933 then: the open 0.1 covered three items and one left, so two thirds remain. See presentation.md. 19 Oct 2026: the DF03/C2C8 vertex group (the target aircraft model in the air-to-air camera inset, 0.1% of vertices in one of 17 recordings) is fixed: `rerun.c` now moves an orientation as one attitude in whichever angle spelling is nearer, because the game stores a model pitched through the vertical as heading and roll half a turn away (that made the in-between picture twist the model about 177 degrees); the group goes from 96.05% to 100% within tolerance, mean error 0.82 to 0.31 px, the whole-flight figure unchanged, and every route stays exact (full gate, all 46 routes in rerun mode, boot N=4/9). Also fixed: weapon attitude cells. Raised from 0.933 to 0.97; what remains is the playback-clock default (simulation: freezes 1 to 0, skips 8 to 0, picture age 73.4 to 71.2 ms at 0.4 / 0.025; the owner's decision) and his visual judgement (Phase 4 maybe). 19 Oct 2026, closed (1.0): the clock default 0.4 / 0.025 is adopted (the owner delegated it) on live evidence: hidden owner-flight replays, two runs per setting, gave 14-15 against 25 freezes and 5-8 against 15-16 skips on the roads flight, 17 and 12 against 21 and 17 on the sharp flight; with the app limited to 8, 4, 2 and 1 CPU cores every run kept up with the whole flight (all in-between pictures drawn, 16 fallbacks) and the new default had 1-4 freezes against 9-12; a simulation sweep over the real step times puts 0.4 / 0.025 on a plateau (0 freezes, 0 skips, 71 ms picture age; higher alpha buys 2-3 ms), so skips against picture age needs no further tuning. The owner's windowed A/B of the roads flight, new against old, looked the same, and he accepted the mission-start low-resolution moment (about 100 ms) as it is. Not scored: refresh rates above 60 Hz and the hardware-only parts (Phase 4 maybe).

P3.item: Flight replays: save a sortie and watch it back (other cameras in Remastered)
P3.evidence: 29 Oct 2026, branch p3-settings-menu. Every live session was already recorded (sessions/session-<time>/ with input.log and the starting save). New: --watch latest or a session name replays one in the window from a scratch copy of its save (watch-save), leaving the player's saves untouched and recording nothing; the settings menu has a Watch last flight row that restarts into it. Run window-less on the 24 Oct recording: it picked the newest session, showed the recorded mission briefing, saves unchanged. Choosing a flight: the menu's Watch a flight screen lists the recorded sessions, newest first with date and log size, and restarts into the one picked (run in the real app with scripted keys: the second flight in the list gave --watch session-20261024-191045, and a run of that name replayed it with the saves untouched). While watching: + and - change the speed (a quarter to 16 times; measured at half speed the clock ran at 30.0 million instructions a second and at a quarter speed 15.0, as 60 million times the speed gives), 0 returns to normal, the sound is off away from normal speed, Ctrl+Alt+P pauses (it already did), and Ctrl+Alt+R starts the replay again (restart run in dry-run mode: it printed the relaunch with --watch latest). Faster than real time is limited by the emulator, about 32 million instructions a second in the heavy part of a flight here. Seeking: ] jumps 30 seconds on (the machine runs flat out, muted, to there: in the real app a 30 second jump of a flight recorded at 60 million instructions a second took about 52 seconds on this machine, the emulator's limit), [ starts the replay again at 30 seconds earlier (--seek SECONDS; dry-run printed --seek 16.61 for a replay 46.61 seconds in). Not done: jumping to a typed time or a marker, other cameras (Remastered), the menu row's restart not run end to end, a flight recorded under a different fix set not examined.

P3.item: Accessibility: subtitles for the speech, full remapping, a colourblind-safe HUD option in Remastered
P3.evidence: 30 Oct 2026, branch p3-settings-menu. Full keyboard remapping (remap = Q:W, --remap, a Remap a key screen in the settings menu). Subtitles for the radio calls (--subtitles, subtitles = yes, a menu entry; src/host/subtitles.c): under the Roland and PC-speaker drivers the speech reaches the speaker as PIT counter 2 counts that follow SPEECH.117's bytes; the detector correlates the latest counts with a stretch from the middle of each of the nine words (the start of a burst runs up to 15 samples out of step), using only what the host already sees of the speaker and the player's own SPEECH.117. Checked: a unit test (all nine words, with and without the stray first event, six chained phrases including all nine in a row, the line expiring, noise finding nothing) and the real thing: a recorded Roland flight replayed in the real app showed Cleared at clock 2,344,005,572 (0.26 s after the speech began) and Cleared for take off 0.5 s later, drawn over the picture. Not done: AdLib (the speech is OPL writes there), the PC speaker driver itself was not run, a colourblind-safe HUD (Remastered), the owner has not looked.

census._about: Historical census from tools/reimp_names.py. matched_bytes: census bytes inside instructions matched code runs (lockstep and route evidence); matched_functions: rows wholly credited; partial_functions: rows in part. supplemental: executed and reviewed static instruction bytes outside those rows in all 17 game code files; added to numerator and denominator for scoring. Strictly validated SETUP XOR code is included by physical byte union; floating LZEXE decompressor and unreviewed static discoveries remain outside. gameplay (21 Oct 2026): the gameplay score's figures over the executed bytes only (denominator: every validated route-executed instruction byte; matched_route_run; stays_original_reviewed; fixture_only; remaining; checklist of previous-scope bytes outside the denominator with and without a docs/reference-reviewed.tsv entry). Refreshed by tools/progress.py --census FILE --named-cover DIR --route-cover DIR --data DIR.

supplemental.basis: census plus executed and reviewed static code in all 17 game code files

gameplay.basis: every instruction byte a validated route capture executes in the 17 game code files
